problem: Vision-language models and RL agents struggle to ground complex concept classes (determiners such as 'few', 'those', and prepositions such as 'above', 'between') to visual targets and compose them for novel instructions. Prior RL grounding work (Hill et al.) covered only small attribute-noun tasks and did not test compositional generalization to held-out instructions.
motivation: Children learn determiners and prepositions incrementally by age three and generalize them to novel situations, while machine agents lack this compositional grounding. Synthetic 3D environments give precise control over train/test splits and class balance, which real-world datasets do not. The paper asks whether a human-like curriculum lets RL agents learn and recompose these concepts.
key_idea: Train an A2C vision-language agent in synthetic 3D navigation rooms with determiner and preposition instructions, using a curriculum from few to all concepts to obtain sample-efficient learning and compositional generalization.
insight: Direct training on eight prepositions fails to converge after 3.5M episodes (24.8% held-out test success, near the 25% chance level), whereas the 4P→8P and 2P→4P→8P curricula converge (2.87M and 2.18M episodes) and generalize (~76% zero-shot). Curriculum is therefore essential when the combinatorial space is large. Pretraining on P and fine-tuning for only 0.1M episodes on the 160,000-instruction D+P environment reaches 53% success, showing that learned concepts transfer and recompose.
method: Synthetic Unity 3D environments: D (8 determiners, 200 instructions), P (8 prepositions, 6000 instructions), D+P (160,000 instructions). Four target locations in a fixed room, and 5 colors and 5 shapes with randomized object positions.
Non-target design: distractors differ in the determiner or preposition, in color/shape, or in both, forcing true grounding of the concept class.
Reward: +10 for the correct target, -3 for a wrong target, -1 for hitting a wall, -10 for timeout (Tmax=500). Performance criterion: perfect reward in ≥800 of 1000 episodes.

Agent: 128x128 RGB goes through 3 conv layers (3136-d). Instructions are one-hot word slots (3/5/7 slots for D/P/D+P) fed to a 128-d linear layer. These are concatenated into a 256-d mixing layer, then an LSTM, then actor and critic heads. Actions are forward, backward, turn left, turn right. Trained from scratch with A2C and RMSProp, lr 2.5e-4.
Curriculum: 8-concept training is compared to 4→8 and 2→4→8 concept stages. The simple concepts are chosen by the fastest learning curves.

Compositional generalization: 75% of shape-concept combinations are used for training and 25% are held out for zero-shot I.I.D. testing. For O.O.D., a 4P→8P pretrained agent is fine-tuned on D+P for 0.1M episodes.

setting.backbone: Small CNN (3 conv) + one-hot language embedding + LSTM actor-critic (A2C), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Self-generated synthetic Unity environments through RL trial and error; D: 160 train instructions, P: 4800 train, D+P: 0.1M fine-tuning episodes after P pretraining
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move forward / backward / turn left / turn right

numbers.extra: tested right after reaching 80% training success; mean±std over 3 runs
numbers.evidence: Table 4 (zero-shot generalization in D and P): 4D→8D 79.0 ± 0.06

numbers.extra: 2.97M total training episodes; few-shot O.O.D.; 160,000 instruction combinations
numbers.evidence: "with only 2.97M training episodes, the agent achieved an average reward of 7.2 and a success rate of 53% over 1,000 testing episodes"

numbers_note: Custom synthetic benchmarks only. Not a standard navigation benchmark. Episode counts to criterion (Tables 1-2): D 0.87M/0.77M/0.82M for 8D/4D→8D/2D→4D→8D; P >3.5M/2.87M/2.18M.
results: Curriculum cut the training episodes for D by 15% (0.87M→0.77M with 4D→8D) and made P learnable (8P fails at >3.5M; 2P→4P→8P takes 2.18M). Curriculum agents reach 76-79% zero-shot on held-out combinations, near the 80% training criterion. A P-pretrained agent reaches 53% success on the D+P environment with only 0.1M fine-tuning episodes.
limitations: Simple geometric objects, a fixed room and no obstacles limit transfer to realistic navigation.
One-hot templated instructions and a small from-scratch encoder; no pretrained vision or language models; only 3 runs.
The 'simple concept' subsets for the curriculum are hand-picked from learning curves, and the optimal curriculum is not explored.
builds_on: Hill et al. 2020 (grounded language learning agent)
Lin et al. 2023 (compositional learning in RL agents)
